summary: Iteration 39: Manager role scoping (BankEzee Connect). Backend: 8/8 pytest tests PASS covering /api/reports/manager-team-stats (today/this_week/this_month), /api/users/manager-team-members (returns 8 team members incl. 1 TL 'Nagulapally pinky' for Teja), and /api/files/ scoped for manager (46 team files). GP role correctly forbidden (403) on team-members endpoint. Frontend: Manager (teja@bankezee.com/tejasme12) correctly redirects to /manager. Team Dashboard renders tiles Calls/Connected/Leads/Files (46) with Today/This Week/This Month filters (verified switch works). Team Overview shows 8 Team Members, 1 Team Lead, 0 Active Today. Files Performance table renders GP-wise breakdown (GP Name, Files, Login, Appr., Disb., Amount) with Nagulapally pinky (TL) badge, 32 files. Call Activity by GP table also present. My Team page (/manager/team) renders 'All Members' + 'Nagulapally's Team' filter tabs, shows Team Leads section (Nagulapally pinky - 5 members, 32 files) and Growth Partners (6) with per-GP stats. Manager Files page (/manager/files) shows 'Team Dashboard' header with 'Manager' badge, and report buttons Sales & Ops / Rejected Cases / GP Performance / Quality / Policy / Commission are visible. GP name badge lookup is client-side using users map (source_name derived from users[source_id]).

minor.issue: Not scoped for manager role - returns system-wide 514 total_files/96 disbursed for Teja instead of team-scoped counts. This causes the Files page top-stat cards to show 514 while the actual files list (which IS scoped) shows only 46. Either both should be team-scoped, or both system-wide - current state is inconsistent.

integration_issues.flow: Manager Files page stats vs list
integration_issues.issue: Top dashboard tiles (Total Files 514, Login 328, Approved 117, Disbursed 96, Total Approved 17.75Cr, Amt in Pipeline 7.14Cr, etc.) show system-wide numbers while the list below shows 'Files (46)' (team-scoped). Confusing UX for managers. Consider using /api/reports/manager-team-stats or scoping /api/files/dashboard/stats when caller is a manager.

issues: Persistent React hydration warnings from dev instrumentation wrapping <tr>, <tbody>, <option>, <select> with <span data-ve-dynamic style='display:contents'> - invalid HTML nesting. Pre-existing since iteration_37/38, not blocking, but pollutes console.

action_items: Decide desired scoping for manager on Files page top-stat cards (/api/files/dashboard/stats): scope to manager's team OR keep system-wide but update Files list to match. Current mixed state (514 in cards vs 46 in list) is confusing.
critical_code_review_comments: reports.py `get_manager_team_stats` includes admin/ops path but description says 'This endpoint is for managers only' and returns {'error':...} instead of raising HTTPException(403) for unauthorized users - inconsistent with users.py `get_manager_team_members` which raises 403. Standardize error handling.

reports.py `get_manager_team_stats` inserts `user_id` (manager's own id) into team_ids but manager's own row is not added to user_map, so manager's own calls/leads/files get counted into totals but do NOT appear in gp_performance/gp_call_stats lists - manager's own activity is invisible in the breakdown.

users.py `get_manager_team_members`: `disbursement_pipeline` uses `disbursed: True` flag but also matches on `eligibilities.disbursed_amount`; if flag is missing/false on records with disbursed_amount, they won't be counted. Verify data consistency.

files_crm.py `get_files_dashboard_stats` (or equivalent) does not appear to filter by manager scope - manager sees 514 system-wide files count in dashboard tiles. Add manager scoping mirroring the list endpoint.

reports.py line 1305-1526 (`get_manager_team_stats`) is 220 lines and re-implements aggregation logic that likely overlaps with existing daily/reports endpoints - consider extracting shared aggregation helpers.
Both endpoints run 4 aggregations sequentially for team members (users.py); consider asyncio.gather like reports.py for consistency and perf.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all acceptance criteria met; one UX inconsistency flagged)
